expectations.text: Treats a speaker who has missed a deadline as stuck rather than uninterested
expectations.evidence: The diagnosis says the 'sorry, chaotic month' reply 'suggests the speakers are stuck, not uninterested'. The response then acts on that reading: it makes the ask small ('takes two minutes', 'use my CFP bio', 'any clear photo... even a phone photo'), offers a fallback, offers to renegotiate ('If that deadline is impossible this week, tell me today'), and gives the 'chaotic month' speaker a personal two-line reply instead of the form letter.

I'd rather print something imperfect than leave you out', and gives the 'chaotic month' speaker a lighter ask ('No stress. Send me one line and a selfie'). It also says 'Skip apologies and guilt' and frames the fallback as 'better for the speaker than nothing, so it isn't a threat'.
